title: Bootstrapping SDK probe-lab: cheatcodes & 10-minute recovery patterns
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact, tactically-oriented notebook for fast bootstrapping and triage when a new team starts integrating Redwood SDKs. Focus: get a reproducible minimal flow that surfaces the 80% friction points and give engineers a handful of "cheatcodes" (patterns + commands) to get back to green within 10 minutes.

Audience:
- Developer Advocates running workshops
- Solutions engineers doing customer onramps
- Internal devs pairing with customers for first-integration bugs

Constraints / assumptions:
- Customers usually start with web + node or python backend, sometimes mobile.
- We assume they have an API key and a small prompt prototype.
- Network issues and telemetry gaps are the most common delays; auth/cors and missing SDK wiring second.

How to use this note:
- Start at "Probe checklist". If you identify a failure mode, jump to the matching quick patch card.
- Run the minimal repro steps while screen-sharing. Keep a terminal open to run the diagnostic curl/snippets.

Probe checklist (run top-to-bottom, expect 2–4 minutes):
- 1) Confirm API key & tier: curl to /v1/health with header Authorization: Bearer <key>. Check 200 + plan in body.
- 2) Local env sanity: echo $REDWOOD_API_KEY; node -e "console.log(!!process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY)" or python -c "import os; print(bool(os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')))"
- 3) Network path: curl --resolve api.redwood.ai:443:<region-ip> https://api.redwood.ai/v1/ping --verbose to see TLS and route.
- 4) SDK wiring smoke: run the minimal sample (below) that sends a single generation; capture request/response latency and error.
- 5) Telemetry check: confirm SDK emitting event types: start_request, end_request, error_event (look for logs in the dashboard or local stdout).

Minimal repro samples (copy-paste):
- Node minimal (paste into quick-repl):
  const fetch = require('node-fetch');
  (async ()=>{
    const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', {
      method:'POST',
      headers:{'Authorization': `Bearer ${process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY}`,'Content-Type':'application/json'},
      body: JSON.stringify({model:'redwood-small', input:'Hello world'})
    });
    console.log(await res.text());
  })()

- Python minimal:
  import os, requests
  r = requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', headers={'Authorization':f"Bearer {os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')}"}, json={'model':'redwood-small','input':'hello'})
  print(r.status_code, r.text)

Common failure modes + quick patches (cards):
- A) 401 / missing key: Quick patch:
  - Confirm header spelled exactly Authorization: Bearer <key>.
  - If environ shows key but request 401: try a freshly minted key, check key scope in console, check that org is not suspended.
  - Temporary workaround: use a test key from the workshop team account (link in linked_artifacts).

- B) CORS / browser blocked requests:
  - Pattern: frontend fetch -> 0 status or opaque error.
  - Patch: proxy requests through backend dev server; use the SDK server-side sample. Instruct frontend to never send API key directly.
  - Quick dev test: curl from the dev machine to replicate the request.

- C) Silent timeouts (SDK returns no telemetry):
  - Probe: run with REDWOOD_SDK_DEBUG=1 to get logs.
  - Patch: ensure outbound port 443 is allowed; if corporate firewall, attempt curl --resolve trick to force route.
  - If logs show socket timeout at 5s: bump client timeout to 15s for initial trials and file a follow-up for improving default.

- D) Unexpected model output or hallucination in early tests:
  - Pattern: prompt truncated, or newlines stripped.
  - Patch: verify encoding; try sending content as plain text vs structured JSON; test with max_tokens reduced. Provide example prompt template we prefer (see examples below).

Telemetry & instrumentation heuristics (for 1st day):
- Minimal events to wire: request_id, model, route, latency_ms, token_count, error_code.
- Add a short-lived dashboard: "first-200-requests" showing latency P50/P95, error rate, top error codes.
- If customer can only send logs: provide a simple parser script (one-liner) to extract request_id and status from logs.

Cheatcodes (one-liners / scripts):
- Fresh key test: curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}s" -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health
- Show last 5 SDK debug lines (if using node): tail -n 200 /tmp/redwood-sdk.log | rg "request_id" | tail -n 5
- Quick local proxy to avoid CORS: npx http-proxy --port 8080 --target https://api.redwood.ai

First-10-minute workshop flow (facilitator script):
- 0:00–1:00: Intro & verify keys (run health curl together)
- 1:00–3:00: Run minimal sample in pair (node or python)
- 3:00–5:00: If error, run probe checklist, pick card, apply quick patch
- 5:00–8:00: Wire minimal telemetry, confirm at least one request shows up in console
- 8:00–10:00: Iterate prompt and show streaming/latency behavior; capture feedback to linked ticket

Examples & prompt template (copyable):
- System: "You are a concise assistant who returns JSON with keys: answer, score. Keep answer <= 120 chars."
- User: "Summarize the following text in one sentence: <paste>"

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Add a tiny browser sandbox that demonstrates recommended proxy pattern (investigate minimal wasm proxy option).
- Provide a single-click test key generator for workshops (security review required).
- Improve default client timeout for SDK when running in ephemeral dev mode.

References & follow-ups:
- Link to onboarding confluence (in linked_artifacts).
- File a small bug ticket for default timeout (ENG-1423).

Quick log of an actual triage I ran (for pattern recognition):
- Customer: workshop with mobile devs, error: opaque CORS in devtools.
- Quick steps I ran: health curl (200), local node sample (401) -> found race: CI-applied key rotated and env was stale -> swapped key -> success.
- Lesson: always verify key freshness first.

If you copy this doc for a different team: replace sample model names with their pinned model and add region-specific endpoints.

-- Maya (quick lab lead)
